title: When does a scene reconstruction become a digital twin?
dek: Reconstruction recovers geometry, appearance, cameras, or changing structure from observations. A digital twin adds the structure needed to inspect, simulate, or act on a scene.
intro: A captured kitchen may look convincing from a new camera view yet provide no collision surface. It may have accurate geometry and still omit a drawer's motion. Reconstruction is not one destination; it is a set of choices about cameras, surfaces, radiance, point maps, time, and physical structure.

Those choices matter because people use reconstructions differently. A photographer may want novel views. A robot may need relocalization, a stable map, free space, or joints that can be simulated. Similar-looking demos can therefore carry very different promises.

We follow a practical progression: establish a common frame; recover visible appearance and shape; keep a map coherent as the camera moves; then represent parts and state when interaction is the goal. Each step adds useful structure, and each adds assumptions worth testing.

sections.heading: Recover a common geometric frame
paragraphs: Multi-view reconstruction begins by relating observations. COLMAP estimates camera poses and sparse structure from image collections, then supplies multi-view stereo tools [cite:colmap-sfm]. RGB-D pipelines can use depth directly: BundleFusion jointly estimates globally optimized poses and reintegrates surfaces online [cite:bundlefusion].

The two routes begin with different evidence. Image-only capture needs overlap and correspondence; RGB-D provides measured depth but still has to track the camera and maintain consistency. A sparse coordinate frame can be extremely useful for alignment while remaining far from a complete surface or an object that can be manipulated.

sections.heading: Represent appearance and geometry differently
paragraphs: NeRF optimizes a continuous field of density and view-dependent radiance for novel-view synthesis [cite:nerf]. Instant-NGP changes the speed tradeoff through multiresolution hash encoding, while Mip-NeRF 360 targets unbounded, anti-aliased scene rendering [cite:instant-ngp] [cite:mipnerf360]. 3D Gaussian Splatting instead optimizes explicit anisotropic Gaussian primitives and uses splatting for real-time radiance-field rendering [cite:gaussian-splatting]. Both may produce compelling novel views, but neither formulation automatically promises a watertight mesh or a simulation interface.

Neuralangelo pursues high-fidelity surfaces from RGB imagery, making a different tradeoff [cite:neuralangelo]. Render quality, surface fidelity, metric accuracy, and scene-specific optimization answer related but separate questions. A system may explain photographs beautifully while never exposing a collision surface, an object identity, or a physical parameter.

sections.heading: Predict geometry without a long optimization
paragraphs: Feed-forward approaches aim to infer useful structure from one or many views without fitting a scene from scratch. DUSt3R predicts dense point maps from uncalibrated image collections and supports camera recovery through global alignment [cite:dust3r]. VGGT predicts cameras, point maps, depth maps, and tracks with a transformer [cite:vggt].

The useful question is what survives after the forward pass. Dense point maps support correspondence and geometry, but a long-lived map may still need fusion, uncertainty handling, or another representation. MASt3R ties dense local matching to metric point maps and global alignment [cite:mast3r]. Learned priors can fill in weakly textured areas, but a plausible surface is still an inference rather than a measurement.

sections.heading: Map while the camera moves
paragraphs: A robot does not receive a finished image collection. It receives an observation stream and must estimate pose while updating its map. iMAP jointly learns a scene-specific implicit map and RGB-D poses online [cite:imap]. NICE-SLAM uses a hierarchical grid-based implicit representation, while SplaTAM couples online RGB-D tracking and mapping to a Gaussian scene representation [cite:nice-slam] [cite:splatam].

Online mapping turns global consistency into a systems problem. Loop closures, drift, compute budgets, and moving objects decide whether a map stays useful. GO-SLAM combines pose estimation, loop closing, and continuous surface updates [cite:go-slam]. A deployable map should distinguish unseen space, revised geometry, and dynamic objects instead of quietly absorbing them into a static world.

sections.heading: Account for time and interaction
paragraphs: Static-scene assumptions fail when a person opens a cupboard or when an object moves. D-NeRF models temporal deformation for non-rigid dynamic rendering [cite:dnerf]. MonST3R estimates per-timestep geometry from dynamic scenes, and 4D Gaussian Splatting combines a canonical Gaussian representation with learned temporal deformation [cite:monst3r] [cite:four-d-gaussian-splatting]. A time-varying appearance model is valuable, but it does not necessarily supply a causal description of motion.

An interactive twin asks for still more: parts, joints, states, and sometimes an executable asset. PARIS recovers part-level shape, appearance, and motion from multi-view observations in two states; DigitalTwinArt uses two RGB-D scans in different states [cite:paris] [cite:digital-twin-art]. These outputs connect reconstruction to functional perception and manipulation, but they should not be confused with a generic photorealistic scene model. A well-rendered door may still lack an estimated axis, allowable range, handle location, or collision behavior.

A video of a moving object gives us another way to recover its structure. Articulat3D follows 3D points through the video, groups their motion, and refines a kinematic model of the parts and joints [cite:articulat3d]. VideoArtGS estimates depth, camera poses, and 3D tracks from a monocular clip, then fits Gaussian geometry and an articulation-based deformation field together. It recovers geometry, part segmentation, and joint parameters in the same process [cite:videoartgs].

sections.heading: Separate observed geometry from completed geometry
paragraphs: Every reconstruction combines evidence with an inductive bias. Classical multi-view geometry gets support from repeated image observations, but loses coverage in textureless or occluded areas. Learned systems can infer likely depth or complete surfaces beyond a measurement, yet their completion is a hypothesis. The distinction is important for a robot: planning through an unobserved gap and planning around an observed free-space volume are not equivalent decisions.

A useful system should retain provenance where possible. Which surface came from a depth measurement, which from multi-view agreement, which from a learned prior, and which changed after global pose correction? Such distinctions help a downstream planner decide when a predicted surface is adequate for visualization and when to request another view. They also make errors diagnosable rather than presenting a single seamless mesh or radiance field as ground truth.

This is a natural point of connection to perception. Semantic labels, instances, and functional parts can guide reconstruction toward relevant structure, while reconstruction gives those predictions a persistent frame across views. Neither direction makes the other redundant: a semantic map can identify a cabinet, but it cannot supply its unobserved back surface; a dense reconstruction can recover surfaces without telling a policy which one is a handle.

sections.heading: Build a model that can run in a simulator
paragraphs: Articulated reconstruction makes the interaction contract concrete. Ditto uses interaction to build digital twins of articulated objects; URDFormer constructs articulated simulation environments from real-world images; REACT3D recovers articulations for interactive physical scenes; and Real2Code explores reconstruction through executable code [cite:ditto] [cite:urdformer] [cite:react3d] [cite:real2code]. Their shared target is not a single rendering format, but a representation in which objects, joints, and state can be inspected or changed.

The hard cases make the difference from view synthesis plain: hidden hinges, coupled parts, unknown friction, and furniture blocked by nearby clutter. A twin may be structurally plausible yet physically wrong. It should make clear which structure came from observations, which was inferred, and which needs another view or controlled interaction.

sections.heading: What should we measure in a reconstruction?
paragraphs: The table separates goals that are often conflated in demonstrations. It is not a performance ranking: an application may reasonably need fast view synthesis, a globally stable map, or an editable articulated state.

callout.title: Rendering is evidence, not the whole contract
callout.text: A compelling novel view demonstrates image consistency under the evaluated view distribution. It does not alone demonstrate metric geometry, complete semantics, connectivity, collision behavior, or action success.

sections.heading: Carry scene structure into generation and action
paragraphs: A reconstruction is most useful when its representation exposes what the later system needs. Generation can use layouts, geometry, scene graphs, and asset constraints to propose varied environments. An embodied agent can use persistent instances, navigable free space, functional parts, and uncertainty to decide whether it can act or must observe again. The same scene may require a radiance model for visualization and explicit structure for planning.

Recent survey work on 4D spatial intelligence similarly separates low-level attributes, scene components, dynamic scenes, interactions, and physical constraints. That hierarchy is a useful guard against calling a visual reconstruction a complete world model [cite:survey-4d-spatial]. The next chapter turns to the complementary question: how can generation create worlds that preserve these structural and interaction-relevant constraints?

takeaway: Ask reconstruction methods for the artifact you need: cameras and point maps for alignment, surfaces for geometry, radiance for rendering, online maps for operation, or parts and joints for interaction. A digital twin is an explicit downstream commitment, not a synonym for a beautiful rendering.
